claims.claim: In MLE-bench, the best-performing setup, OpenAI's o1-preview with AIDE scaffolding, achieves at least the level of a Kaggle bronze medal in 16.9% of competitions.
claims.quote: the best-performing setup--OpenAI's o1-preview with AIDE scaffolding--achieves at least the level of a Kaggle bronze medal in 16.9% of competitions.

claims.claim: A Claude v3 Opus agent achieved a 37.5% average success rate on MLAgentBench.
claims.quote: It can build compelling ML models over many tasks in MLAgentBench with 37.5% average success rate.

claims.claim: MLAgentBench success rates ranged from 100% on well-established older datasets to 0% on recent Kaggle challenges potentially created after the LM was trained.
claims.quote: the success rates vary considerably; they span from 100% on well-established older datasets to as low as 0% on recent Kaggle challenges created potentially after the underlying LM was trained.

claims.claim: The best pairing of search strategy and operator set increased the MLE-bench lite Kaggle medal success rate from 39.6% to 47.7%.
claims.quote: Our best pairing of search strategy and operator set achieves a state-of-the-art result on MLE-bench lite, increasing the success rate of achieving a Kaggle medal from 39.6% to 47.7%.

claims.claim: MLE-STAR achieved medals in 64% of Kaggle competitions on MLE-bench Lite and significantly outperformed the best alternative.
claims.quote: Our experimental results show that MLE-STAR achieves medals in 64% of the Kaggle competitions on the MLE-bench Lite, significantly outperforming the best alternative.

claims.claim: The best-performing tested agent on MLRC-Bench closed only 9.3% of the gap between baseline and top human participant scores.
claims.quote: Even the best-performing tested agent (gemini-exp-1206 under MLAB [22]) closes only 9.3% of the gap between baseline and top human participant scores.

claims.claim: Evaluations of eight frontier LLMs found that current models still had significant limitations in autonomously generating long-horizon solutions and efficiently resolving complex errors.
claims.quote: Extensive evaluations of eight frontier LLMs reveal that while current models achieve meaningful iterative improvements, they still exhibit significant limitations in autonomously generating long-horizon solutions and efficiently resolving complex errors.

open_questions: These sources leave open how often LLM agents produce correctly running programs versus merely achieving partial benchmark success, because several report medal or success rates without separating runnable-code correctness from score improvements.
The sources do not provide a common baseline or directly comparable success-rate measurement across MLE-bench, MLE-bench Lite, MLAgentBench, and MLRC-Bench.
